title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask favours and permission politely, invite people, accept and refuse gracefully, and use Sindhi honorifics correctly.
intro:
Sindhi courtesy has many layers. Beyond **توهان** and **تون** there is the very respectful **پاڻ** (pāṇa, literally 'self'), used to and about highly respected people; there are request forms in **-jo** (ڪجو، اچجو) that sound gentle and warm; and there is a whole ritual of offering and refusing that every guest needs to know.

In this unit you'll learn to make requests at different levels of politeness, ask permission with the **subjunctive** ('may I…?'), and invite, accept and decline.

vocab.note: Takes plural verbs: پاڻ ڪڏهن آيا؟ 'When did you (sir) arrive?' Also reflexive 'self'.
Direct form اوهين avhīṃ. Common in writing, speeches and some regions.

phrases.en: Sorry to bother you — may I ask something?

phrases.native: ڇا توهان منهنجي مدد ڪري سگهو ٿا؟
phrases.roman: chhā tavhāṃ munhinjī madada karī sagho thā?

phrases.en: Would you please close the window.
How can I help you, sir? (lit. give your order)
Come and have a meal with us.

phrases.native: توهان جي دعوت آهي، ضرور اچجو.
phrases.roman: tavhāṃ jī daʿvata āhe, zarūr achijo.

phrases.en: Of course, thank you! What time?

phrases.native: معاف ڪجو، اڄ نه اچي سگهندس.
phrases.roman: māf kajo, aʄu na achī saghandus.

Thanks, there's no need. / No thanks.

phrases.native: مان توهان جو ڏاڍو ٿورائتو آهيان.
phrases.roman: māṃ tavhāṃ jo ɗāḍho thorāito āhiyāṃ.

phrases.en: Now please allow me to leave. (polite way of saying goodbye)

grammar.title: Levels of request
grammar.body:
From blunt to most courteous:

1. **Bare stem** (intimate): ڏي ɗe 'give', ويهه veha 'sit' — only to close friends and children.
2. **-o** (polite): ڏيو ɗiyo, ويهو veho — normal with توهان.
3. **-ijo / -jo** (gentle, deferential, or for later): ڏجو ɗijo, ويهجو vehijo, ڪجو kajo — sounds soft and caring; also used for advice and instructions to be followed later ('do call when you arrive' = پهچي فون ڪجو).
4. **مهرباني ڪري** + polite form, or a question with **سگهو ٿا** 'can you…': ڇا توهان … ڪري سگهو ٿا؟

Add **سائين / ادا / ادي** at the end and a softening **ٿورو** 'a little': ٿورو انتظار ڪجو 'please wait a moment'.

**Highest respect**: use **پاڻ** (pāṇa) for 'you' or 'he/she' when speaking to or about an elder, scholar or saint, with plural verbs: پاڻ ڪٿان آيا آهيو؟ 'Where have you (respected sir) come from?'

examples.en: Do call when you get home. (gentle)
When did you (honoured sir) arrive? (very formal)

grammar.title: Asking permission and offering: the subjunctive
grammar.body:
The **subjunctive** is the present-tense form **without ٿو** — مان اچان, اسين هلون, هو ڪري. On its own, as a question, it means **'may I / shall I / shall we …?'**:

اندر اچان؟ 'May I come in?'
هڪ ڳالهه پڇان؟ 'May I ask something?'
چانهه آڻيان؟ 'Shall I bring tea?'
هلون؟ 'Shall we go?'

It's also used after **ته** for wishes and suggestions: مان چاهيان ٿو ته توهان اچو 'I'd like you to come'; بهتر آهي ته اسين هاڻي هلون 'it's better that we go now'. And in blessings: خدا توهان کي خوش رکي 'may God keep you happy'.

**Refusing politely**: thank first, then give a soft reason: مهرباني، پر … · ضرورت ناهي · وري ڪڏهن 'another time' · بس، ڪافي آهي 'that's enough'. Expect a host to insist at least once!

examples.en: Shall I make you some tea?

examples.native: بهتر آهي ته اسين هاڻي هلون.
examples.roman: bihtaru āhe ta asīṃ hāṇe halūṃ.
examples.en: It's better that we leave now.

examples.native: مهرباني، پر مون کي دير ٿي رهي آهي. وري ڪڏهن.
examples.roman: meharbānī, para moṃ khe dera thī rahī āhe. varī kaɗahiṃ.
examples.en: Thanks, but I'm getting late. Another time.
May God keep you happy! (blessing / thanks)

dialogue.title: A visit to a Sindhi home
dialogue.setting: John is invited to the home of his colleague's father, Ghulam Hussain, in a village near Hala.

lines.speaker: Ghulam Hussain
lines.native: ڀلي ڪري آيا، سائين! اندر اچو، ويهو.
lines.roman: bhale kare āyā, sāīṃ! andari acho, veho.
lines.en: Welcome, sir! Come in, sit down.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: مهرباني، سائين. مون توهان لاءِ مٺائي آندي آهي.
lines.roman: meharbānī, sāīṃ. moṃ tavhāṃ lāi miṭhāī āndī āhe.
lines.en: Thank you, sir. I've brought some sweets for you.

lines.speaker: Ghulam Hussain
lines.native: ان جي ڪهڙي ضرورت هئي! پاڻ آيا، اهو ئي ڪافي آهي.
lines.roman: un jī kahiṛī zarūrata huī! pāṇa āyā, uho ī kāfī āhe.
lines.en: There was no need for that! That you came is enough.

lines.speaker: Ghulam Hussain
lines.en: (to his son) Son, bring the ajrak.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: اوهه! هيءَ ته وڏي عزت آهي. مان ڏاڍو ٿورائتو آهيان.
lines.roman: oh! hīa ta vaɗī ʿizata āhe. māṃ ɗāḍho thorāito āhiyāṃ.
lines.en: Oh! This is a great honour. I'm very grateful.

lines.speaker: Ghulam Hussain
lines.en: Will you have tea or lassi?

lines.speaker: John
lines.en: Tea, please. But only a little sugar.

lines.speaker: Ghulam Hussain
lines.native: ماني به تيار آهي. ٿورو ٻيو وٺو، شرمائو نه!
lines.roman: mānī bi tayāru āhe. thoro ɓiyo vaṭho, sharmāo na!
lines.en: The food is ready too. Have a little more — don't be shy!

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: بس سائين، ڪافي آهي. پيٽ ڀرجي ويو.
lines.roman: basi sāīṃ, kāfī āhe. peṭu bharje vayo.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: هاڻي اجازت ڏيو. توهان جي مهمان نوازيءَ جي مهرباني.
lines.roman: hāṇe ijāzata ɗiyo. tavhāṃ jī mehmān navāzīa jī meharbānī.
lines.en: Now, please allow me to take my leave. Thank you for your hospitality.

culture: Hospitality in Sindh is sacred. A guest (مهمان) is fed first and best, and the highest honour is to be draped with an **ajrak** or given a **Sindhi topi**. Guests are typically received in the اوطاق in villages. It is polite to bring a small gift (sweets, fruit) when visiting, to refuse a second helping once before accepting, and to ask permission to leave (اجازت ڏيو) rather than just announcing departure. In very formal or religious settings you'll hear **پاڻ** for 'you' and Persian-style phrases like تشريف آڻڻ 'to grace (a place) with your presence'.
